proposed_takeaway: Adopted on 7 July 2026 for public consultation until 30 October 2026. The guidelines confirm that the GDPR applies to collection, storage, organisation and retrieval of scraped personal data, require purpose limitation, transparency and minimisation, recommend timestamping and validation for accuracy, clarify legitimate interest as the basis for training, and require both a GDPR Article 6 basis and an Article 9 exception for special-category data, citing GC and Others (C-136/17) for incidental collection with safeguards. They complement the copyright policy and training-content summary duties in Article 53. Providers scraping for training should align data governance with them now, before the final version.
note: Art 53(1)(c) exists and is the copyright policy duty; 53(1)(d) is the training-content summary, so the Article 53 claim holds. Only the unlabelled GDPR Article 6 and 9 citations could be misread in an AI Act digest.
Art 10 is data and data governance and Art 59 is further processing of personal data in the sandbox, exactly as the takeaway uses them; Art 2(7) is the data protection savings clause.
Art 53 is the GPAI provider obligations and Art 2(7) the relationship with Union data protection law; both bear on a taskforce report about a GPAI provider.
Art 26 deployer duties matches the takeaway's own claim and Art 2(7) is the data protection savings clause; Art 4 AI literacy is the loosest of the three but still bears on staff use guidance.
Art 70(2) does carry the 2 August 2025 publication deadline and Art 77(2) the 2 November 2024 fundamental rights list; Art 99 is penalties.
Art 70 covers the market surveillance authority and single point of contact, Art 57 the national sandbox and Art 99 the penalty regime.
Art 70 and Art 99 fit the designations and penalties; Art 57 is sandboxes, which the Italian law provides for even though the takeaway does not spell it out.
AESIA as market surveillance authority and single point of contact is Art 70, the national sandbox pilot Art 57 and the penalty regime Art 99.
Art 70 for the sectoral market surveillance authorities and single point of contact, Art 28 for the four notifying authorities and Art 77 for the fundamental rights authorities.
Art 70, 74(8) and 77 all hold; Art 74 has 14 paragraphs and (8) is the DPA-as-market-surveillance provision.
Art 70 covers designation and single points of contact; Art 77 covers fundamental rights authorities.
Articles run 1 to 113 and the consolidated text has exactly Annexes I to XIV.
